_readme: Card data for projects.html. Each project's 'id' must match the 'project:' label in Zotero's Extra field. 'end': null means ongoing with no end date ('present'). 'status' is 'ongoing' or 'completed'. 'summary' may contain simple HTML links. 'extra_outputs' are outputs not (yet) in Zotero.

projects.title: Acerta Chair AI at Work
projects.summary: How can organisations use AI to make work more meaningful, autonomous and accessible? The chair studies three routes: employees crafting their own jobs with generative AI, organisations redesigning repetitive tasks with automation, and AI-supported knowledge sharing that lets non-experts take on specialised tasks. It combines surveys and small field experiments in organisations, and it supports a PhD project by Melissa Gheyle (2025–2029).

facts.label: Partners
facts.value: Co-chairholders Rein De Cooman and Sophie De Winne

projects.title: BEL-AI: Leveraging AI for Belgium
projects.summary: Evidence for Belgium's ambition to become a "Smart AI Nation". The project maps Belgium's AI research, investment and adoption gaps, then studies whether AI raises productivity, how firms adjust their workforce, and how AI changes skill needs, autonomy and job quality for workers. A final pillar turns the findings into policy recommendations with policymakers, social partners and industry, to support AI diffusion while managing the risks for workers.

facts.label: My role
facts.value: Overall project lead; leads several work packages; main proposal writer

projects.title: WELFAIR: Intergenerational fairness and the welfare state
projects.summary: How do inequality, technological change and demographic change affect fairness between generations? WELFAIR builds an indicator of intergenerational fairness to compare countries and social groups, and develops a social investment policy framework.

facts.label: Partners
facts.value: Coordinated by the European University Institute; 13 partners

facts.label: My role
facts.value: Task leader (two tasks); contributor to other tasks

projects.title: AI exposure and productivity
projects.summary: Which jobs can AI partly do, and what is happening to the people who hold them? The project builds a single EU AI exposure score from existing measures, separating substitution from support. It then looks at wages, employment and working conditions in the most exposed occupations and sectors, and runs a meta-analysis of the productivity literature.

facts.label: My role
facts.value: Task leader (Task 1); contributor to Tasks 2 and 3; main proposal writer

projects.title: AI and youth employment
projects.summary: How is AI affecting young people's jobs, and entry-level jobs in particular? This study for the European Commission covers the EU27 from 2019 to today and looks ahead to 2035. It measures which sectors and entry-level jobs are exposed to AI, looks at working conditions and new tasks, reviews EU policy and legislation, and builds future scenarios, drawing on surveys of businesses and young people.

facts.label: Partners
facts.value: Led by Open Evidence, with ICF; CEPS and RPA as subcontractors

projects.title: Uneven diffusion: why AI does not spread equally
projects.summary: AI is often seen as one technological wave centred on a few hubs. This project tests whether cities instead build AI specialisations on their existing industries, using data on publications, patents and startup investment. The aim is a framework for regional smart specialisation in the AI era.

facts.label: My role
facts.value: Senior Fellow, co-lead with Pierre-Alexandre Balland

projects.title: Trends in non-standard work
projects.summary: Current classifications miss how insecurity in contracts, working time and income can pile up in one job. The study develops an updated typology of non-standard employment and uses EU-LFS, EU-SILC and EWCS data to look at job creation since 2010, economic well-being and working conditions.

facts.label: My role
facts.value: Task leader (Task 4); contributor to Tasks 1 and 5

projects.title: AI and early careers in Europe
projects.summary: US studies find falling employment for young workers in AI-exposed roles. This project is a first European replication, using payroll data from Acerta (2021–2025) combined with sectoral AI exposure measures developed at CEPS. It compares Europe with the US and asks whether European labour market institutions soften the effect. A book chapter presents the sectoral measures; the working paper with the replication is in progress.

facts.label: My role
facts.value: Senior Fellow, co-lead with Pierre-Alexandre Balland

extra_outputs.title: Working paper on AI and early careers in Europe

projects.title: Independent expert on AI, technological change and the future of work
projects.summary: Commissioned research and expert advice for European institutions and agencies on how AI, and technology more broadly, changes work. My work looks at two levels: the labour market, including occupational change and skills, and the organisation of work, including job design and organisation design.

projects.title: A social and inclusive Europe in the next decade
projects.summary: A synthesis of research on the changes facing the European Pillar of Social Rights and the ESF+, covering future skill needs, skill supply, equality of opportunity and inclusion. The goal was to help target ESF+ funding.

projects.title: European Ecosystem of Excellence in AI
projects.summary: The EU has no coordinated approach to AI development, which leaves a fragmented ecosystem. The project mapped Europe's AI landscape, built datasets on AI jobs and industrial specialisation, and ran foresight workshops, podcasts and events on a future-ready workforce.

projects.title: Generative AI and the future of work dialogue (GPAI)
projects.summary: Roundtables and interviews in Asia, Europe and Latin America on what generative AI means for working conditions, future skills and job design.

projects.title: GI-NI: Growing inequality
projects.summary: How do technological change, globalisation and migration together affect work, skills and inequality in Europe? GI-NI measured these effects and developed policy options for inclusion.

projects.title: Labour market projection model for Flanders
projects.summary: A forecasting model for the Flemish labour market at Steunpunt Werk. It matches projections of labour demand and supply across sectors, occupations and skills to map future shortages and mismatches, so that education, training and lifelong learning can be better aligned with labour market needs.

projects.title: Future of Work and Inclusive Growth in Europe
projects.summary: A research-to-action project on how AI and technology affect work, welfare systems and inclusive growth, with four strands: new technologies in the workplace, new ways of working, reskilling and mobility, and an inclusive digital economy. The project built a network of academics, policymakers and businesses, and a Future of Work dashboard.

projects.title: MANUWIN: workplace innovation in industrial manufacturing
projects.summary: Seven Flemish manufacturers redesigned their work organisation with support from Workitects. The project developed data-driven tools for information flow mapping, team design, team KPIs and workability measurement.

projects.title: IAO woonzorg: workplace innovation in residential care
projects.summary: Twenty residential care homes went through a change process towards a new way of organising work, aiming at better care for residents and workable jobs for staff. Workability was measured at the start and end with the Werkmeter survey.

projects.title: WIFI2020: workplace innovation in food manufacturing
projects.summary: Seven food companies in two learning networks moved from hierarchical to more self-organising structures. Nine companies took part in the Werkmeter workability survey: among 400 employees, average workability rose by 10% and the need for recovery fell by 12%.

projects.title: PhD: Exclusive dealing and foreclosure in the automotive industry
projects.summary: Do exclusive contracts between car makers and their dealers keep new competitors out? Using a spatial model of consumer demand for new cars, the PhD estimated whether exclusive dealing raises entry costs for new manufacturers and gives domestic firms an advantage. A second study looked at net neutrality and online innovation in the UK. Defended in June 2015.
